title: Microbiota DNA Isolation and 16S rRNA Sequencing for Rodent Fecal Samples
author: Love, Gubert, et al.
materials: Platinum Hot Start PCR master mix

This step aims to extract genomic DNA from the previously collected fecal samples. Ensure appropriate PPE is worn during the extraction process.7.Extraction of genomic DNA in fecal samples:a.In a biosafety cabinet, take ∼25 mg of mouse fecal sample and prepare the genomic DNA using the QIAamp PowerFecal Pro DNA kit as per manufacturer’s instructions (QIAGEN).b.For the positive control, thaw and vortex the ZymoBIOMICS Microbial Community Standard (Zymo Research) to ensure even mixing. Take 30 μL of the microbial standard and add to a PowerBead tube containing C1 buffer provided in the kit.c.For the negative control, add in 50 μL of nuclease-free water to a PowerBead tube containing C1 buffer provided in the kit.d.Perform bead beating at 5,000 rpm for 30 s on Precellys 24 tissue homogenizer (Bertin Instruments) or equivalent homogenizer to ensure complete lysis of the sample.e.Follow the manufacturer’s instructions for the remaining steps and elute the extracted DNA with 85 μL of nuclease free water. Troubleshooting 2.8.Quantify the extracted DNA using Qubit dsDNA HS assay kit, Quant-iT PicoGreen dsDNA Assay kit or equivalent.9.Assess the purity of the extracted DNA by measuring the A260/230 and A260/280 ratio using Nanodrop.Note: This protocol describes the steps for the processing of fecal samples using QIAamp PowerFecal Pro DNA kit. Other kits that could be used for manual preparation include QIAGEN DNeasy PowerSoil Kit, or QiaSymphony PowerFecal Pro DNA kit. It is important to choose kits specifically for extracting genomic DNA from fecal or soil material to enable efficient lysis and to eliminate inhibitors of downstream sequencing applications that are commonly found in fecal samples.

steps.title: Prepare labeling and animal housing
steps.instruction: Clearly label all collection tubes for fecal samples; verify that the appropriate versions of R and all required R packages are installed; ensure all mice are housed in the same experimental room with consistent light/dark cycles and controlled temperature and humidity.

steps.title: Collect fecal pellets
steps.instruction: In a biosafety cabinet, weigh approximately 25 mg of each mouse fecal pellet for DNA extraction.

steps.title: Set up computational environment
steps.instruction: Use R version 4.1.0 on a computer with a 3.1 GHz Dual‑Core Intel Core i5 processor and 16 GB 2133 MHz LPDDR3 memory; install the following packages with the indicated versions: biomformat V1.20.0, dada2 V1.20.0, phyloseq V1.36.0, ggpubr V0.4.0, ggplot2 V3.3.6, mixOmics V6.16.3, nlme V3.1‑158, vegan V2.6‑2, DECIPHER, phangorn, gghighlight, dplyr.

steps.title: Extract DNA from fecal samples
steps.instruction: Follow the QIAamp PowerFecal Pro DNA kit (QIAGEN) manufacturer’s protocol for each ~25 mg fecal pellet.

substeps.instruction: Add the sample to a PowerBead tube containing C1 buffer.
For the positive control, thaw and vortex the ZymoBIOMICS Microbial Community Standard (Zymo Research), take 30 µL and add to a PowerBead tube with C1 buffer.
For the negative control, add 50 µL nuclease‑free water to a PowerBead tube with C1 buffer.
Bead‑beat all tubes at 5,000 rpm for 30 s using a Precellys 24 tissue homogenizer (or equivalent).
Continue with the kit’s remaining steps and elute the DNA in 85 µL nuclease‑free water.

steps.title: Quantify and assess DNA purity
steps.instruction: Measure DNA concentration using either the Qubit dsDNA HS assay kit or the Quant‑iT PicoGreen dsDNA assay kit (or equivalent). Assess purity by recording A260/230 and A260/280 ratios on a Nanodrop spectrophotometer.

steps.title: Note DNA extraction timing
steps.instruction: The DNA extraction step requires approximately 5–7 hours for 94 samples plus 2 controls.

steps.title: Process raw sequencing data
steps.instruction: Upload Illumina MiSeq FASTQ files to the Qiita platform; run the default quality‑control pipeline to demultiplex, trim, and generate amplicon sequence variants (ASVs).

steps.title: Load R libraries for analysis
steps.instruction: In R, execute: library(biomformat); library(dada2); library(phyloseq); library(ggpubr); library(ggplot2); library(mixOmics); library(nlme); library(vegan); library(DECIPHER); library(phangorn); library(gghighlight); library(dplyr).

steps.title: Import ASV table and filter brain samples
steps.instruction: Read the ASV count table saved as a ‘.biom’ file from the data folder using the biomformat package; remove any rows corresponding to brain samples that were included in the .biom file for a different study.

steps.title: Import and factor sample metadata
steps.instruction: Read the sample information file; convert qualitative variables into factors for Genotype, Housing, Sex, Box, Sex_Geno, and Housing_Geno.

steps.title: Create phyloseq object
steps.instruction: Construct an OTU table (ASV) with taxa_are_rows = TRUE, a taxonomy table from the taxa classification file, and a sample data object; combine them into a phyloseq object: physeq <- phyloseq(ASV, TAX, sampledata).

steps.title: Build phylogenetic tree
steps.instruction: Using DECIPHER and phangorn, obtain sequence names, align them (phang.align), build a neighbor‑joining tree (treeNJ), fit a maximum‑likelihood model (fit = pml(treeNJ, data = phang.align)), then fit a GTR model (fitGTR); add the tree to the phyloseq object with phy_tree(fitGTR$tree) and set seed 711 for reproducibility.

steps.title: Transform counts to relative abundances
steps.instruction: Create a relative‑abundance phyloseq object: physeq_ra <- transform_sample_counts(physeq_count, function(x) x / sum(x)).

steps.title: Inspect library sizes
steps.instruction: Extract library size per sample, plot with ggplot2 and gghighlight to flag samples with <20 000 reads (e.g., Sample 65); do not remove flagged samples.

steps.title: Rarefy to uniform depth
steps.instruction: Rarefy all samples to 15 000 reads using physeq.rarefied <- rarefy_even_depth(physeq_count, rngseed = 1, sample.size = 15000, replace = FALSE). Note that the lowest original library size is 17 871 reads.

steps.title: Calculate alpha diversity metrics
steps.instruction: Using phyloseq’s estimate_richness, compute observed species richness, Shannon index, and Inverse Simpson index for each sample (these correspond to the metrics used in Gubert et al., 2022).

steps.title: Test alpha diversity differences
steps.instruction: Run ANOVA models in R: summary(aov(Observed ~ Housing + Sex + Genotype, data = alpha_div.df)); repeat for Shannon and InvSimpson.

steps.title: Compute beta diversity distances
steps.instruction: Using the non‑rarefied physeq_ra object, calculate Bray‑Curtis distance (distBC <- phyloseq::distance(physeq_ra, method = "bray")) and Unweighted UniFrac distance (distUF <- UniFrac(physeq_ra, weighted = FALSE, normalized = TRUE, parallel = FALSE)).

steps.title: Visualize Bray‑Curtis PCoA
steps.instruction: Ordinate Bray‑Curtis distances with PCoA, then plot using ggplot2 with custom shape (c(16,1,17,2)) and fill colors ("#F8766D","#619CFF","#00BA38"), set text size to 16 and point size to 4.

steps.title: Visualize UniFrac PCoA
steps.instruction: Ordinate Unweighted UniFrac distances (ordUF <- ordinate(physeq_ra, method = "PCoA", distance = distUF)) and plot similarly with custom shapes, fills, text size 16, and point size 4.

steps.title: Perform PERMANOVA on beta diversity
steps.instruction: Run adonis2 on Bray‑Curtis: adonis2(distBC ~ Housing + Sex + Genotype, data = data.frame(sample_data(physeq_ra))); repeat for Unweighted UniFrac: adonis2(distUF ~ Housing + Sex + Genotype, data = data.frame(sample_data(physeq_ra))).

steps.title: Filter low‑abundance ASVs
steps.instruction: Add an offset of 1 to the entire ASV matrix to avoid zeros before centered log‑ratio transformation; define a function low.count.removal(data, percent = 0.01) that keeps ASVs whose column‑sum proportion exceeds the percent threshold; apply to the full dataset and separately to female and male subsets.

steps.title: Generate PCA plots by sex
steps.instruction: Create PCA objects (pca.result) from filtered data; plot overall PCA with plotIndiv(pca.result, group = filterASV_16S$indiv$Housing, title = "PCA plot", pch.levels = levels(filterASV_16S$indiv$Sex_Geno), pch = c(16,1,17,2), legend = TRUE, ind.names = FALSE, legend.title = "Housing", legend.title.pch = "Gender_Genotype", col = c("#F8766D","#00BA38","#619CFF"), level.colors = levels(filterASV_16S$indiv$Housing)). Then plot sex‑specific PCAs with ellipses for females and males using the respective filtered datasets.

steps.title: Run sPLS‑DA on female HD data
steps.instruction: Filter female samples with genotype “HD”: female_hd.16S <- filterASV_16S.female.pca$indiv %>% filter(Genotype == "HD"); set response Y <- female_hd.16S$Housing and predictor X <- filterASV_16S.female.pca$filter.data.raw[rownames(female_hd.16S),]; tune the model with set.seed(2543) and tune.splsda.female_hd (specify ncomp and select.keepX); fit splsda.female_hd; plot individuals with plotIndiv(..., ellipse = TRUE); plot loadings for components 1 and 2 with plotLoadings(..., comp = 1) and plotLoadings(..., comp = 2); compute overall and class‑wise error rates via perf.plsda.female_hd and perf.plsda.female_hd$error.rate.class.

steps.title: Visualize PCA with cage effect
steps.instruction: Plot the overall PCA colored by cage/box number using plotIndiv(pca.result, group = filterASV_16S$indiv$Box, title = "PCA plot with Cage", ind.names = filterASV_16S$indiv$Box, cex = 1.5, style = "lattice").

steps.title: Fit linear mixed models on CLR data
steps.instruction: Transform raw counts to centered log‑ratio (CLR) values for each sex; fit separate linear mixed‑effects models (using nlme) with Housing and Genotype as fixed effects and Cage (Box) as a random effect to test associations with ASV abundance.

steps.title: Note bioinformatic timing
steps.instruction: The complete bioinformatic analysis and data visualization requires approximately 3–5 hours.

description: 1.Clearly label all tubes for fecal collection.2.Ensure you have access to the appropriate versions of R and the relevant packages.3.Ensure all mice are housed in the same experimental room with the appropriate light/dark cycles and controlled for temperature and humidity.
